item.title: Health Ministry Seeks IS 126 Million to Strengthen Clinics and Village Health Posts
item.description: The primary-care line in the draft 2027 budget would pay for equipment, training and a drug reserve, with the aim of easing pressure on the Regional Hospital in Talas.

item.title: Cotton Picking Ends at a Record 41,000 Tonnes on the Rim and the Chu
item.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources says the 2026 raw-cotton crop is the largest in its records since 2007, helped by a summer of steady canal water.

item.title: Moscow Honours Compatriots' Leader in Bishkek; Nurzhan Notes the Neighbour's Council
item.description: The Russian president has decorated the head of Kyrgyzstan's Russian compatriot organisations, a model with no equivalent in Irad.

item.title: Camera Traps Record Two Snow Leopards in Upper Besh-Tash, a First in Decades
item.description: Rangers, TSU scientists and Akjele elders are working out how to keep the cats and the returning flocks apart.

item.title: Uzbek Workers Abroad Halve as Remittances Quadruple; Irad Sees a Familiar Economy
item.description: Tashkent reads the shift as a rise in skilled labour, while Irad's own money from abroad keeps flowing home through Talasbank and Tulpar Pay.

item.title: Migrants' Families Say Cost of Sending Money Home Matters More Than Wages
item.description: With Uzbekistan pressing for bigger remittances, Iradi households that rely on pay from Russia and Kazakhstan are weighing routes, fees and exchange rates.

item.title: Uzbek Grandmaster Beats Three Top Rivals in US Before Title Match; Nurzhan Takes Note
item.description: The neighbouring win lands in Irad's chess city, where players rated under the FIDE flag wonder what an Iradi world-class flag would look like.

item.title: US Transshipment Report Names No Iradi Firm; Talas Watches Origin Rules Abroad
item.description: A White House paper on third-country trade routes touches the paperwork Irad's exports already travel on, and the Ministry of Economy says it is following its neighbours' lead.

item.title: Uzbek Grandmaster Wins US Tournament; Nurzhan's Chess Fans Ask Whose Flag
item.description: A neighbour's last-day victory before the world title match leaves Irad's chess city asking what flag one of its own players would carry.

item.title: After a Comic's Apology to Kazakhstan, Irad Recalls Its Own Screen Portraits
item.description: A British comedian's apology to the Kazakh people has Talas remembering the Swift Hooves cowboys, Homer's kazy and a film it cannot watch at home.

item.title: Kyrgyz Wrestler Wins World Silver in Astana; Irad Again Counts Its Mat Talent Abroad
item.description: A silver for Kyrgyzstan's women's team at the Astana worlds is welcomed in Talas, where Iradi wrestlers compete under neighbours' flags.

item.title: Uzbek Diplomat Named Turkic States Secretary General; Irad Eyes the Rim
item.description: Uzbekistan's deputy foreign minister takes the post for the first time, and Talas weighs what a neighbour's gain means along the 145-km Fergana frontier.

item.title: Neftchi Win Kara-Ak Derby 2–1 to Take Irad League Title by a Point
item.description: Neftchi Nurzhan overturned a two-point deficit on the last day to finish on 63 points, one ahead of Tulpar Talas.

item.title: Rim Villages Get Tap Water 11.4 Hours a Day, TSU Survey Finds; District Pledges Tank
item.description: A university survey of three Fergana-rim villages finds the 2021 water scheme runs well short of round-the-clock supply, and Lower Naryn says it will fund the missing storage in the 2027 budget.

item.title: Offshore Exchange Hack Puts Tulparcoin's 3.59-Cent Quote Under the Spotlight
item.description: A reported $6.3 billion cyberattack at a major foreign exchange revives the Bank of Irad's September warnings on the coin.

item.title: Central Asia's Power Demand to Rise 27% by 2030; Toktogul Eyes Winter Value
item.description: Regional analysts expect demand to climb sharply by the end of the decade, and the ISEZ's 1,440 MW dam sits just outside the planning that will answer it.

item.title: Bishkek Completes 327 km of Border Fence; Irad Reads It Against Its Own Open Frontier
item.description: Kyrgyz officials say the engineering works on the Tajik border are finished, while Irad's frontier with Kyrgyzstan relies on posts, pillars and informal contact.

item.title: Toktogul Exports Hit 99% of Plan as Bishkek and Tashkent Talk Power
item.description: While the Kyrgyz and Uzbek energy ministers discuss electricity supply, Irad's dam is steady, its contracts on schedule and its reservoir 87.6% full.

item.title: Heating Runs in Talas and Nurzhan as Old Mains Face First Cold Weeks
item.description: Radiators are warm in both big cities, repair crews are on call, and officials say the Soviet-era mains are ready for winter.

item.title: Turkic States Meet in Ankara to Pitch Transit Routes; Irad Follows From Outside
item.description: Turkey used the Organization of Turkic States summit to promote itself as the western end of Central Asia's freight corridors, and Irad's traders have their own stake in the outcome.

item.title: TSU Finds Bronze Age Settlement and Painted Horses Near Kara-Suu Canyon
item.description: A summer survey in the Talas Alatau foothills has uncovered stone house foundations and about 40 red-ochre figures, mostly horses and riders, at a site now fenced off while recording continues.

item.title: Sary-Bulak Plans 146 MW Small-Hydro Cascade on the Chatkal River
item.description: District head Taalaibek Imashev told residents that Iradenergo would buy the output of a chain of small stations, the first at the Chatkal valley mouth.

item.title: Sary-Bulak Counts $216.6 Million in Mining Investment as Antimony Revival Gathers Pace
item.description: District officials tell the Lieutenant Governor that pledged and spent money in antimony since 2024 has reached US$216.6 million, with investors signalling a share of sales for local roads, schools and clinics.

item.title: Nine Housing Complexes, 3,308 Flats Rise in Four ISEZ Cities for 2027–28 Handover
item.description: City halls in Talas, Nurzhan, Iyık Janyl and Kyzyl-Adyr say building is on schedule, while the edge-of-city fields some sites occupy prompt a debate.

item.title: Record Harvest Lifts ISEZ Farm Output to IS 6.1 Billion in Nine Months
item.description: Volume is up about 12% on last year, but the potato glut held the rise in value to about 6%, the Ministry of Economy's preliminary estimate shows.

item.title: Maksat Proposes Small Refinery at Kochkor-Ata to Bring Fuel Closer to the South
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor told Lower Naryn residents the government wants a 450,000-tonne plant to supply the southern districts, a plan to be studied rather than a decision.

item.title: Record 700 Gather in Nurzhan for NurGaz Oil and Gas Conference
item.description: Attendance rose about 40% on last year at the Palace of Metallurgists, where talk of Irad's gas ran well ahead of any decisions.

item.title: 495 New Flats Rise in Western Talas, Due for Handover in 2027
item.description: City Hall says eleven nine-storey blocks are going up for families buying with bank mortgages.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Plan Driverless Truck Trials; Irad Watches Its Busy Crossings
item.description: Neighbouring plans for automated freight on the Kazakh–Chinese route leave Irad outside the corridor, but not outside the trade.

item.title: Tash-Kömür Coal Yards Busy as Households Stock Up for Winter
item.description: Mine management says supplies will last the heating season, even as Kyrgyzstan caps coal prices and smog readings climb.
